newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope greets pilgrims, resumes full duties Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Pope greets pilgrims, resumes full duties Sunday.

text.p: Pope John Paul greeted pilgrims at the Vatican on Wednesday in a brief appearance ahead of his return on Sunday to a full programme of activities following an appendix operation.

The 76-year-old Pope, who is still convalescing, appeared briefly at the window of his apartment overlooking St Peter's Square to greet pilgrims in Italian, English, French, German, Spanish and his native Polish.
His weekly Wednesday audiences and Sunday masses have been suspended with other public duties since he entered the Gemelli Hospital in Rome on October 6.
Surgery was successfully carried out on October 8 and the Pope returned to the Vatican on October 15.

The Pope will resume his public activities on Sunday when he says mass at St Peter's to mark the 350th anniversary of the 1646 Union of Uzhorod, which sealed the return of the Eastern Orthodox Ruthene Church to union with the Roman Catholic Church.

On November 1, the Roman Catholic feast of All Saints, he will celebrate the 50th anniversary of his ordination as a priest. He is scheduled to say mass at St Peter's Basilica that day with all the priests of Rome.
